g.text: THE OUT-OF-BAND SAFETY INTERLOCK: DUAL-CHANNEL HARDWARE POWER DISCONNECT
Deterministic Hardware Boundary: Electromechanical Contactors, Redundant Safety Relays, and Safe Torque Off (IEC 61800-5-2)
breaks contacts even if lightly welded.
• Cat 4: Single fault does not degrade safety.
Generates non-overlapping 1 ms test pulses to detect cross-wire shorts:
Series feedback through NC contacts of K1, K2 and motor contactors.
If any contact welds shut, the EDM loop stays open, latching reset lockout.
ISO 13849-1: Category 4, PL e | IEC 62061: SIL 3
3. Actuator Inverter Stage & Safe Torque Off (STO)
Galvanic Gate-Driver Isolation & Motor Stator Inverter
Electromechanical Spring-Applied Friction Brake Interlock (Category 0 Stop)
When STO trips, the brake solenoid de-energizes simultaneously. Heavy mechanical springs
clamp friction pads onto the rotor shaft in 15–40 ms, arresting rotation and preventing drop.
Architectural Invariant: Complete Separation from AI Software & Schedulers
Under IEC 61800-5-2 and ISO 13849-1, Safe Torque Off (STO) is an unprogrammable physical safety function. Even if the unprivileged Linux OS, neural network inference engine,
or real-time scheduler crashes, hangs, or experiences an arithmetic memory overflow, the hardware STO disconnect path guarantees that gate-driver bias current is zero.
